name: CowAgent
vibe_summary: A massively popular open-source personal AI assistant and 'Agent Harness' that plans tasks, runs skills, and self-evolves with memory and knowledge. Multi-agent, multi-model, and multi-channel with a one-line install and an active skill hub.
best_for: Users wanting a 24/7 personal assistant across IM platforms
Builders extending agents via a skill hub and plugins
avoid_if: You need OS-level sandboxing for tool execution
You want a minimal, auditable codebase
You require strict offline-only operation guarantees
openclaw_advantages: Very large community and 47k+ stars with active maintenance
Skill Hub and one-line install lower the barrier to extension
Broad multi-channel IM support out of the box
Self-evolution features: long-term memory and knowledge base
openclaw_disadvantages: Python runtime is heavier and slower to boot than lean alternatives
Computer-control and shell access increase attack surface
Security model appears application-level rather than OS-isolated
Feature breadth may mean more config and dependency complexity

overview_markdown:
CowAgent is an open-source personal AI assistant positioned as a reference implementation of 'Agent Harness' engineering. It proactively plans tasks, controls the host computer and external services, creates and runs Skills, and maintains a personal knowledge base with long-term memory. It supports multi-agent teams, multiple LLM providers, and deployment across the web and major IM platforms, with a one-line install and a dedicated Skill Hub for extensions.

Recent commits show active engineering focused on efficiency and reliability: prompt caching for Claude requests with configurable TTL, context trimming that preserves cacheable prompt prefixes, and a steady stream of community-contributed fixes across memory, model catalog, web search, and config handling. The project ships regular releases (v2.2.0 as of late September 2026) and maintains docs, a Discord, and a WeChat community.

Compared to OpenClaw, CowAgent emphasizes self-evolution (memory, dream diary, evolution logs) and a broad skill ecosystem, while sharing the same general risk profile: deep computer control and shell access without strong OS-level sandboxing. It is a strong choice for users who want a hackable, community-driven assistant, but those prioritizing isolation and minimal attack surface may prefer containerized or Rust-based alternatives.
